reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage BUSD X3/X4 as a joining opportunity requiring a payment, which is divided among participants, and describes earnings through participant and team activity, including adding members. Although the speaker notes that some participants earned nothing for three months, the presentation still includes claims of earning without work and an earnings account associated with adding 27 members; actual payments and displayed balances are not verified.

citations.quote: FORSAGE BUSD X3 X4 FULL PRESENTATION ZOOM CLASS IN URDU
we need 13 dollars for level 1 joining
After you get this $13, we will go to the joining process
You will earn even if you do not work and team work.
there are people in our team who have gone through the non-working profit system within an hour

opening.argument: Judge, the earnings discussion includes a concrete counterexample to easy-profit claims: the speaker says some participants "have not earned a dollar for three months" and tells listeners who expect non-working profit to "make sure we work here." Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the presentation promises effortless returns. The speaker also emphasizes retaining wallet information over time. This is an imperfect explanation of a risky activity, but its own account does not present earnings as certain or immediate.

citations.quote: these people have not earned a dollar for three months
make sure we work here
this 12 ki is very important for you people

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited joining price establishes a cost, not a guaranteed return. And the opening's quote about earning without work omits the same discussion's example of people earning nothing for three months. The speaker's claimed experience may be unverified, but lack of independent verification does not by itself show that this presentation promises everyone the same outcome.

citations.quote: we need 13 dollars for level 1 joining
some such people are also there that these people have not earned a dollar for three months

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging that some people earn nothing does not change what is being offered. The presentation describes earnings even without work alongside a paid entry and payments distributed when people join. Those are features of the promoted arrangement, not merely a discussion of financial risk.

citations.quote: You will earn even if you do not work and team work.
After you get this $13, we will go to the joining process
As soon as registration is made in the system, the blockchain verifies the payment and it will automatically divide into two parts.

opening.argument: Judge, this is structured as a class explaining an unfamiliar system. The title calls it a "FULL PRESENTATION ZOOM CLASS," and the speaker walks through wallet preparation, payment routing, and the X3/X4 positions. He says viewers should learn first and act afterward, then explains why particular payments go to other positions. Even the earnings discussion includes participants who made nothing for three months. The stronger reading is an operational demonstration whose claims can be examined, not evidence that every viewer is being promised a result.

citations.quote: FORSAGE BUSD X3 X4 FULL PRESENTATION ZOOM CLASS IN URDU
we will learn everything first, then we will do it after learning
So what is X3 and X4? We will talk a little here because many people ask the question that what is X3 and X4?
these people have not earned a dollar for three months

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies real joining and payment mechanics, but explaining mechanics is exactly what a class about this system would do. Its quoted non-working earnings claim is qualified in the surrounding account by people who earned nothing for months. The opening does not show that the diagrams or reported earnings independently verify any payment.

citations.quote: You will earn even if you do not work and team work.
some such people are also there that these people have not earned a dollar for three months

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A classroom format does not make the subject merely academic. The speaker moves from preparation to a specific joining process, describes payments to the person whose link brought in a participant, and says adding a member produces earnings. The caveat about unsuccessful participants does not erase that recruitment-based earning mechanism.

citations.quote: After you get this $13, we will go to the joining process
So the link to which someone joined, then his payment will go to him.
you entered one person in the system, you earned five dollars, your appliner earned five dollars

opening.argument: Judge, the stated transaction is a joining payment whose allocation the speaker attempts to explain, rather than an unexplained demand for money. He specifies a level-one cost and says the entry payment is split between X3 and X4 positions. He also concedes that some people earned nothing for months, so the account does not establish a guaranteed return. This record supplies a description of a paid referral-based business activity; it does not independently establish whether the displayed payments occurred or whether the service is legitimate. That uncertainty should not be converted into a finding of deception.

citations.quote: we need 13 dollars for level 1 joining
soon as you enter the system then at the same time your 10 dollars are divided into two parts
these people have not earned a dollar for three months

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes a joining fee and participant-linked payouts, but neither its quotes nor the account's unverified earnings claim establishes a guaranteed return or proves the described transfers occurred. The speaker expressly acknowledges unsuccessful participants. The narrower conclusion is that this is an explanation of a paid referral arrangement, with its actual performance unresolved.

citations.quote: we need 13 dollars for level 1 joining
these people have not earned a dollar for three months

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is not merely that a paid service lacks independent verification. The speaker says a new participant's payment goes to the person whose link they used, identifies commission from later participants, and ties his claimed earnings to recruiting 27 members. A warning that some people earn nothing makes the risk clearer; it does not turn these recruitment-linked payouts into ordinary product sales.
